steps: Dice the onion and bell pepper and mince the garlic.
Soften the onion and bell pepper in a wide pan, then add the garlic, the cumin, paprika, cayenne and caraway and fry a minute until fragrant - cumin and caraway together are the Tunisian signature.
Pour in the tomato sauce, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer 10 minutes until thick enough to hold a spoon trail.
Make wells in the sauce and crack the eggs into them.
Cover and cook 5-8 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Crumble the feta over the top and serve with the warmed pita for scooping.

note: Added the garlic it had none of, plus cayenne standing in for harissa's heat and caraway, which with cumin is what makes the spicing read Tunisian rather than generic. The dish is Tunisian/Libyan in origin rather than Levantine, but the Middle Eastern label is defensible and the report did not require changing it.

steps: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of cold water for at least 12 hours. Do not use canned or cooked chickpeas and never boil them - falafel is made from raw soaked chickpeas, and cooked ones turn the mixture to paste that falls apart in the oil.
Drain the chickpeas well and grind them with the onion, garlic, parsley and cilantro to a coarse, sandy texture.
Season with the cumin, coriander powder, salt and black pepper and rest the mixture 30 minutes.
Shape into small patties and shallow-fry in the vegetable oil until deep brown and crisp on both sides.
Slice the cucumber and loosen the tahini with cold water and a little salt into a pourable sauce.
Serve the falafel with the hummus, the tahini sauce, the cucumber and the warm pita.

note: The critical fix is in the method: the step now specifies dried chickpeas soaked raw and never boiled, which is the single thing that separates falafel from a chickpea patty that disintegrates. Added the herbs that give falafel its green interior (fresh parsley and cilantro, both registry rows), plus onion and garlic, and a real frying fat - the recipe previously fried nothing in nothing. Dried Parsley dropped in favour of fresh.

steps: Slice the chicken thigh into strips and marinate it with the greek yogurt, the lemon juice, the minced garlic, the red wine vinegar and the cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, salt and black pepper. Give it at least 30 minutes - the yogurt-and-acid marinade is what makes shawarma tender and is the step that was missing.
Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Sear the marinated chicken hard in a very hot pan without crowding it, so the edges char the way they would coming off the spit.
Slice the cucumber and warm the chickpeas through.
Build the bowl with the rice, the charred chicken, the chickpeas and the cucumber, and spoon the hummus alongside.

note: Added garlic and a proper yogurt-and-vinegar marinade with resting time - the spice blend was already right but was being applied as a dry seasoning at the pan rather than as the marinade shawarma depends on. Both variants updated in step with the base (garlic added to each); the no-yogurt variant marinates in lemon, vinegar and garlic alone. This is the app's only variant recipe, so the variants array is carried through deliberately.

steps: Grate the yellow onion and squeeze the liquid out of it - wet onion makes the kofta fall apart on the grill.
Mix the ground lamb with the grated onion, the finely chopped parsley, the cumin, paprika, coriander powder, allspice, cinnamon, salt and black pepper, and work it until it turns slightly sticky.
Rest the mixture in the fridge 20 minutes, then shape it around skewers or into flattened fingers.
Grill or broil 5-6 minutes per side until charred outside and just cooked through.
Slice the red onion thinly for the garnish and loosen the tahini with cold water into a pourable sauce.
Serve the kofta with the hummus, the tahini sauce, the raw red onion and the warm pita.

note: Added grated yellow onion and fresh parsley to the meat mixture, which is what kafta is - the recipe had red onion only as a garnish and no herb at all. Added allspice and cinnamon, the two warm spices that define Levantine kafta. Kneading to stickiness and resting are now explicit, since both are what hold the kofta together.

steps: Slice the lamb shoulder thinly across the grain and marinate it with the red wine vinegar and the cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, salt and black pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Sear the lamb hard in a very hot pan in batches so it chars at the edges rather than steaming.
Slice the red onion thinly and chop the parsley.
Loosen the tahini with cold water and a squeeze of salt into a pourable sauce.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan, lay the lamb down the middle, top with the red onion, parsley and tahini sauce, and roll it up tightly.

note: Took route B, which Phase A unblocked: shawarma is thin slices carved off a stacked spit, so ground lamb made the name wrong. Lamb Shoulder is now in the registry, so the meat could change instead of the name. Added a vinegar marinade and fresh parsley. Macro-neutral at -1%.

steps: Soak the bulgur in a little cold water for 15 minutes until it softens, then squeeze it dry. Tabbouleh uses only a small amount of bulgur - it is a parsley salad with grain in it, not a grain salad with herbs in it.
Chop the parsley very finely and dice the tomato and cucumber small.
Season the chicken breast with salt and black pepper and grill it, then slice it.
Toss the parsley, bulgur, tomato, cucumber, chickpeas and mint with the olive oil and the lemon juice.
Season, let it sit 10 minutes for the flavours to come together, and serve with the sliced chicken on top.

note: The worst offender in the slice: a dish called tabbouleh with no parsley, no bulgur, no mint and no tomato, built on brown rice instead. Took the report's route A, which Phase A unblocked by adding Parsley, Mint and Bulgur - all three were flagged as unavailable at audit time. Brown Rice removed. Parsley is now the dominant ingredient by volume, which is what tabbouleh actually is. About -14% calories; protein holds at ~55 g.

steps: Char the whole eggplant directly over a gas flame or on a hot grill, turning it, until the skin is blackened all over and the flesh has collapsed. The smoke is the dish - an oven-roasted eggplant makes a dip, not baba ganoush.
Let it cool, then peel off the burnt skin and drain the flesh in a sieve so the dip is not watery.
Mash the eggplant with the tahini, the crushed garlic, the lemon juice, the cumin, salt and black pepper - mash by hand rather than blending, so it keeps some texture.
Spread on a plate, pour the olive oil over the top, and serve with the sliced cucumber and the warm pita.

note: Added garlic, which every version has and this had none of. The real fix is the technique: the step now insists on charring the eggplant whole over a flame until the skin blackens, then draining it. Without the smoke it is just an eggplant dip, and without draining it is a watery one.

steps: Slice the chicken breast into strips and marinate at least 30 minutes with the greek yogurt, the lemon juice, the minced garlic, the red wine vinegar, the olive oil and the cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, coriander powder, cardamom, salt and black pepper.
Sear the chicken in a very hot pan in batches, leaving it alone long enough to char at the edges.
Slice the cucumber and loosen the tahini with cold water into a pourable sauce.
Warm the pita.
Plate the chicken with the hummus, the tahini sauce, the cucumber and the pita.

note: Same core gap as the Shawarma Bowl: the right spices were being used as a dry rub instead of as the yogurt-lemon-vinegar marinade that shawarma is built on. Added the yogurt, garlic and lemon for the marinade and cardamom and coriander to round the blend.

steps: Rinse the brined grape leaves well and pat them dry, trimming off any stems.

Mix the RAW white rice with the ground lamb, the finely diced onion, the allspice, cinnamon, salt and black pepper. The rice must go in uncooked so it swells inside the roll as it absorbs the cooking liquid.
Lay a leaf vein-side up, put a small line of filling near the stem end, fold the sides in and roll it tight but not straining - the rice needs room to expand.
Pack the rolls seam-side down in a snug layer in a heavy pot.
Pour over the olive oil, the lemon juice and just enough water to cover, and weigh the rolls down with a plate so they hold their shape.
Simmer covered on low heat 45 minutes until the rice is tender and the leaves are soft. Serve warm or at room temperature.

note: The dish is named after grape leaves and had none - Grape Leaves is now a registry row, so they are the wrapper at 70 g. The other real fix is that the rice goes in RAW: the old steps implied cooked rice, which gives a dense filling instead of one that swells to fill the roll. Added the weighted-plate step that keeps the rolls from unravelling.

steps: Cube the lamb shoulder and sear it hard in the olive oil until well browned, then set it aside.
Slice the onion and soften it with the minced garlic.
Return the lamb, add the cumin, cinnamon, ground ginger, turmeric, paprika and the saffron, and stir until the spices coat everything and smell toasted.
Add the tomato sauce and about 1 cup of water - just enough to come partway up the meat, since a tagine braises in its own steam rather than boiling in liquid.
Cover and braise gently 1 hour, then add the carrot, eggplant and chickpeas and cook 30 minutes more until the lamb pulls apart.
Season with salt and black pepper and scatter the chopped cilantro over before serving.

note: Relabeled Moroccan - a tagine is named after the Maghrebi vessel it cooks in and is not a Middle Eastern dish. Ground lamb replaced with cubed Lamb Shoulder (Phase A row): a tagine is a long slow braise and mince cannot do it. Cook time raised from a simmer to a 90-minute braise. Dropped the White Beans, which belong to no tagine, and added cilantro and saffron. Liquid rescaled and the braise-not-boil point made explicit. NOTE: Moroccan is a new cuisine label beyond the five pre-approved ones - flagging it rather than assuming.

steps: Pulse the turkey breast in a food processor until coarsely ground, or use ground turkey.
Mix it with the minced garlic, the finely chopped parsley, the cumin, coriander powder, allspice, salt and black pepper, and knead until sticky.
Rest the mixture 20 minutes, then shape it into flattened fingers.
Grill or broil 5-6 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Grate the cucumber, squeeze it dry and stir it into the greek yogurt with the mint - this is khyar bi laban, the Levantine yogurt-cucumber side.
Slice the red onion thinly and serve the kofta with the khyar bi laban, the hummus, the red onion and the warm pita.

note: Added garlic and fresh parsley to the meat mixture (a kofta with neither is just a turkey patty) plus allspice, and made explicit that the turkey has to be ground. The yogurt-cucumber side is now built properly and named khyar bi laban rather than tzatziki, which is Greek - that mislabel was the report's specific complaint.

blocked.did: OMITTED. Sumac is deliberately excluded pending the owner's decision - it is in the same botanical family as cashew and pistachio with documented cross-reactivity. This is the one Middle Eastern recipe that wants it, exactly as CLAUDE.md predicted. Only the owner can decide.

blocked.wanted: Ras el Hanout 3g and Preserved Lemon 10g
blocked.did: neither is in the frozen vocabulary. Used the individual warm spices already present plus Saffron; the tagine reads correctly without them but preserved lemon is a genuine loss worth considering for a future registry pass.
used Mint, the spice-vocabulary name Phase A added.

blocked.did: all five ARE in the registry - Phase A added them. This let Tabbouleh take route A and become real tabbouleh, and let Lamb Shawarma Wrap keep its name via route B instead of being renamed.
